name: CAPGEMINI
description: Capgemini is a consulting company where I have worked primarily on client projects in the energy and telco sectors. My work has focused on back-end development, including building Java-based RESTful microservices with Spring Boot, front-end development with Angular, and, more recently, the use of AI tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code.

clients.description: My first assignment was on a private suite of web applications used by the client's staff to manage third-party bookings of television and radio advertising slots and packages. As a Full-stack Developer, I built Angular 8 features and Java/Spring Boot services exposing RESTFul APIs within a microservices architecture, with Oracle SQL and Spring Data JDBC for persistence. Maven, Jenkins, SVN, and Postman were part of the development and delivery workflow. Since this was my first project, I had to absorb its technologies and processes quickly; by January, I was already handling my assigned tasks independently. The engagement later ended when COVID-period budget cuts required me to move to another project.

I helped build an internal field-service application from scratch to schedule maintenance and fault-resolution work across the client's fibre-optic and copper-pair networks. I worked directly with the client from the outset and independently delivered my assigned front-end work in Angular 11. For the first six months, I focused exclusively on the front end. When the back-end developer left, I took ownership of the full application, expanding into the Java 8/11 and Spring Boot backend, its RESTFul APIs implemented as microservices, and ongoing maintenance. During the engagement I also took part in a one-week, 24-hour on-call rotation approximately every two months, responding to issues across the client's systems with guidance from the systems administrators.

After my earlier assignment, the client explicitly requested that I return to the team. The systems had since evolved, but I was able to rejoin quickly by applying my familiarity with the team's delivery practices. I worked on the client's internal applications as a Full-stack Developer, using Angular 13, Java 11, Spring Boot, Spring Data JDBC, and Oracle SQL; the back-end services exposed REST APIs through a microservices architecture. My contribution also expanded beyond implementation: from early in the engagement I increasingly analysed requirements, decomposed work into tasks, and prepared estimates, taking greater responsibility for shaping work before development began.

On this project, I moved into an Agile front-end team developing web applications to manage and schedule field work on the client's electricity and fibre networks. It was my first experience with Agile delivery. Initially, the team comprised a senior front-end developer and me at middle level. We translated client requirements into interface proposals using Figma and the client's component libraries, presented the designs directly for approval, and then implemented them in Angular, coordinating work through Jira and Git. Because the applications processed large data sets, I also improved table-loading workflows with pagination. In the final six months, I took responsibility for onboarding and training a junior developer who joined as the workload grew; they became productive within a few weeks. I also led substantial front-end refactoring: integrating microfrontends with Module Federation and upgrading Angular from version 12 to 16. In my final month, the client proposed that I take over the senior developer's front-end responsibilities, but contractual constraints between the client and Capgemini prevented the transition.

I returned to back-end engineering, my preferred area, to develop and maintain an application that remotely triggered operations on the client's electrical substation hardware, particularly data-collection tasks. Its services were RESTFul APIs in a microservices architecture, built with Java 17 and Spring Boot and using MongoDB for persistence. I refactored the back-end integration, moving away from an infrastructure in which Apache Camel acted as a proxy between incoming requests and the services. I also added automated tests with JUnit and Mockito.

This engagement introduced me to AWS and cloud services in practice. I wrote Python-based AWS Lambda functions called by the client's batch processes and front-end applications, working with API Gateway, Secrets Manager, and CloudWatch. I also used MongoDB and worked with Terraform, Jenkins, Git, GitHub, Jira, Confluence, and Datadog across development, delivery, and monitoring. Although my role was back-end focused, I was the sole front-end developer and independently owned that workstream, proposing and implementing new features. As most planned client tasks approached completion, I spent the final four months helping onboard and develop the person who would take over my responsibilities. The team held all Agile ceremonies in English.

I joined to replace a senior back-end developer and took ownership of REST endpoints consumed by the client's mobile application. I independently analysed, estimated, and implemented my work in a Java 17/Spring Boot service backed by MongoDB. The test suite used JUnit, Mockito, and WireMock; the delivery toolchain included Gradle, Jenkins, Kubernetes, and Argo. I also took part in interviewing candidates to help recruit developers for the group. Agile ceremonies were conducted in English with colleagues in Egypt. The assignment was brief: following a management change, the client closed several work groups to reduce costs.

I currently develop Java/Spring Boot microservices and REST APIs used by the client's internal web applications, with MongoDB and Apache Kafka among the technologies in the stack. I also build Unix batch jobs scheduled in crontab to update and reconcile data from systems that capture insurance claims reported by operators. One of these jobs migrates sensitive documents between systems. To accelerate implementation, I now use AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code regularly, while reviewing and validating the generated changes.
